extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of classical algebra/geometry (readers of historical Italian mathematical treatises)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for manipulating binomials, trinomials and quadrinomials: testing commensurability, forming squares, multiplying to obtain higher-degree compound expressions, using geometric area interpretations, and finding reciprocals and particular powers by algebraic and geometric constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regola generale per trovare potenze di un binomio
rubrics_metrics.description: "quando tu volelTe trouare la.*^.oeqlunca binomio tc fofié .ppoflo Tempre rie/ n i qfta regola generale farai oel magio: fuo nome ooi tal parti ebe multiplica 'ta vna in lalira faeia la qrta parte od quadrato bel mino" (general rule: to find a given power/quantity of a binomial follow the rule — multiply the named parts one into the other to obtain the fourth part or square of the lesser).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrounding exposition gives examples: pick the two parts (magio: nome and mino: nome) and multiply them in cross to obtain quarter of a square; apply iteratively for higher powers. Several worked numeric/geometric examples illustrate the procedure and how to split lines into parts whose products correspond to quarters of squares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moltiplicare una parte in un'altra per ottenere la quarta parte del quadrato
rubrics_metrics.description: "quando tu volelTe trouare la.*^.oalcun binomio p la data regola vo: rat fare del fuomagte nome doi parti ebe multiplicata vna in laltra l^abia a fare la quarta parte del quadrato de lo mino" (to find the specified binomial do: take the two named parts and multiply one into the other to make the fourth part of the square of the lesser).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained with geometric diagrams: multiplying one segment into another corresponds to area constructions yielding quarter-squares; used repeatedly to reduce binomial problems to constructions with squares and rectangles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uso delle superfici (aree) e dei quadrati come interpreti numerici
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout: frequent identification of "superficie" (area) and "quadrato" (square) of a line with the algebraic square or product of quantities (e.g., "la fuperficie oc vna in laltra ... la radici ..." and "la radici de tutto el binomio muUiplicata in la radici de tutto dfuorecifo").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text uses geometric area language to justify algebraic manipulations (squares and sums of squares, double areas for cross-terms). Examples show translating algebraic products into constructions of squares and their 'supplementi' to reason about binomial powers and residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comporre quadrinomio moltiplicando binomi componenti
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements that multiplying binomials/trinomials produces quadrinomia: e.g., "multiplicando ditto quadrinomio in fe medefimotde Tua quadratura ne guiene radici ..." and descriptions of how squares of components join to form quadrinomia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: multiply component terms pairwise (cross-multiplication), collect resulting squares and cross-terms into the quadrinomial; the treatise gives symbolic/diagrammatic demonstrations showing how component squares and cross-areas assemble into the full quadrinomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regole per l'incrociamento (cross‑multiplication) e il doppio delle superfici
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent rule: for cross-terms take the double of the surface produced by intersection of parts ("per lo doppio de la fupcrficie de vna in laltra ... lo incrociamento ... fera lo doppio de la superficie ...")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to obtain the cross-term coefficient: the 'double' of the rectangle formed by two segments corresponds to 2ab in (a+b)^2 expansions. The text instructs multiplying squares into each other and doubling intersections to get correct composed areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condizioni di incommensurabilità tra componenti e loro potenze
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertions about when two binomial component lines are incommensurable in powers/lengths: e.g., "fra loro incommcnfurabili in lo: pctentiaie... anche in longitudine ... saranno ..." (if component lines are incommensurable, their powers and areas are incommensurable accordingly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reason about irrational components and inability to reduce to common measures; guides whether algebraic simplifications by common factors/denominators are possible, and when one must work with reciprocals or construct geometric analogues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uso dei recíproci (recifò) per determinare quantità corrispondenti
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple passages about the role of reciprocals: "il suo recifo ... a cioe ... il nome del binomio ... il recifo del primo binomio ... il fuo recifo ..." indicate that to each binomial corresponds a reciprocal quantity used in constructions and calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that each binomial has an associated reciprocal quantity; manipulating reciprocals (multiplying, squaring, taking fourth parts) helps produce desired binomials or to compare different binomials' magnitudes; examples show successive reciprocal constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metodo per ridurre a linee commensuranti i termini del binomio
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for making terms commensurate by forming appropriate squares/multiplications and supplementi: e.g., constructing rectangles/supplementary areas to transform incommensurate components into comparable quantities ("la multiplicatione oe lo.it t. cioè c g r.iu lo t b.aoe oe ... la fupfrìe ori fupplcmento").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric constructions (equilateral quadrilaterals, supplements) are recommended to transform problems of incommensurate line segments into ones with commensurable areas so algebraic relations become tractable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ripetizione di moltiplicazioni per ottenere potenze maggiori
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction that to obtain higher powers (e.g., square, fourth, etc.) one should repeatedly multiply the binomial or its components in the prescribed manner: "per multiplicare in fe fa.2  8,cauane la fugficie oc luna in laltra ... poi per hauere la fupcrficie Doppia per li incrociamenti ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work by successive application of the basic cross-multiplication and squaring rules; the text presents sample sequences (square, then square again to obtain fourth power and so on) and how to track resulting terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regole di denominazione e uso dei nomi (magio: nome / mino: nome) nei procedimenti
rubrics_metrics.description: The treatise repeatedly uses naming conventions for parts of binomials ('magio: nome' for the greater part, 'mino: nome' for the lesser) and prescribes using those names consistently in formulas and constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming parts clarifies which term to square, which to multiply crosswise, and which to take as 'meno' for forming remainders; many worked examples show how to apply operations to the 'magio' and 'mino' parts per the general rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comporre figure geometriche (tetragoni equilateri etc.) come rappresentazione delle quantità
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples show building equilateral quadrilaterals and subdividing sides to represent binomial components and their squares: "figura geometrica ... il tetragono equilatero ... la sua radici è ... lo quadrato ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These geometric constructions are used to visualize algebraic identities and guide the arithmetic operations; the text instructs constructing such figures and counting their parts/areas to obtain algebraic results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riduzione e sostituzione per isolare termini incogniti
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural advice for isolating unknowns by forming appropriate combinations (subtracting squares, taking parts) and reducing compound expressions to simpler binomials amenable to the main rule: e.g., using quarter-parts and differences to move from a compound to the desired binomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worked manipulations show reducing a complicated quadrinomial by removing known square-parts and cross-terms to leave a simpler binomial; these reductions often rely on earlier rules (multiply one part into another, take fourth parts, use reciprocals).
